description: Given Dagster resources holding credentials (ConfigurableResource subclasses, EnvVar, built-in integration resources), map each to the matching Orchestra connection type, referenced by name/${{ ENV.* }} in pipeline YAML — never inlined.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset to an Orchestra pipeline task, focusing on how the SnowflakeResource's credentials should be represented (see files/snowflake_resource_asset.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SNOWFLAKE task whose connection: references either a name_XXXXX connection or a ${{ ENV.* }} variable — never the literal account/user/password from the EnvVar calls. warehouse/database/role are not written as task parameters since they belong to the connection, not duplicated per task unless the source genuinely varies them.

assertions.text: The task uses the SNOWFLAKE integration
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT / SNOWFLAKE_USER / SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env var names are not written as literal parameter values in the YAML

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job to Orchestra pipeline tasks, making sure the two Airbyte resources map to the correct Orchestra connection types (see files/airbyte_cloud_and_server.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sync, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Two tasks: one using an Airbyte Cloud-style connection (from AirbyteCloudResource, API-key auth) and one using an Airbyte Server-style connection (from AirbyteResource(host=,port=), self-hosted), each with the correct connection_id from the source, and neither resource's credentials (AIRBYTE_CLOUD_API_KEY, AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER/PASSWORD) written as literal values.

assertions.text: Both Airbyte tasks are distinguished from each other rather than collapsed into one identical connection type — AirbyteCloudResource and AirbyteResource(host=,port=) map to different Orchestra connections
Connection ids 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 and 66666666-7777-8888-9999-000000000000 are carried over as the sync targets (as parameters, not as the connection: name itself)
AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER and AIRBYTE_SERVER_PASSWORD are not written as literal parameter values
